question: Two teams, one seed, no games left against each other - what decides it?

headline.text: Golden State Valkyries and Las Vegas Aces have no meetings left. Golden State closes 2 of 6 at home; Las Vegas closes 3 of 5.

body: Golden State Valkyries and Las Vegas Aces are fighting for the second seed - and they will never see each other again. Zero head-to-head games remain. From here, the race is decided entirely by proxy: by geography, by rest, and by how each team survives Minnesota.

The proxies are not neutral. Golden State closes with two of six at home. Las Vegas closes three of five at home. Two teams separated by 1.5 of a win in our projections, separated by several points of schedule context.

Then there is the Minnesota gauntlet: zero of the highest-leverage remaining games in the league are these two teams against the Lynx -  for Golden State,  for Las Vegas. Split them and the schedule edge probably decides it. Sweep or get swept, and the proxies stop mattering.
Watch the rest columns, not the rivalry - there isn't one left to watch.
